Romeo and Julie is a pleasant but conventionally plotted reflection on working class aspiration, family and love across a divide.

cn.t: Owen's working-class Cardiff spin on Shakespeare proves witty and moving, though only tangentially related to the Bard. Critics praise its sweet-yet-savage portrait of young love amid poverty, but some find it skirts deeper issues.
